query: Build a 3D top-down dungeon crawler with procedurally generated rooms. The dungeon is a grid of interconnected rectangular rooms linked by short corridors. Walls are dark stone-textured boxes, floors are slightly lighter stone tiles with subtle cracks. The player character is a small armored knight (a capsule body with a cone helmet and a rectangular shield on one side) controlled with WASD movement. The knight auto-faces the mouse cursor direction. Left-click performs a sword slash (a quick arc of a flattened box sweeping in front of the character, dealing damage to enemies in range). Right-click throws a fireball (a small glowing orange sphere with trailing particles) that travels in the cursor direction and explodes on contact with an enemy or wall, dealing area damage. Enemies: green slime blobs (sphere shapes that hop toward the player, low HP), skeleton warriors (taller capsules with a bone-colored tint that charge and melee), and a boss bat (large dark winged V-shape that swoops in circles and dives at the player). Each room may contain 2-5 enemies; all must be defeated to unlock the exit doors (iron gate meshes that slide up). Treasure chests (small box shapes with a gold lid) appear randomly, giving health potions or damage boosts. Fog of war: rooms not yet visited are dark, the current room is fully lit with a warm point light centered on the ceiling. Minimap in the top-right corner showing explored rooms. HUD: health bar, fireball cooldown indicator, room count. After clearing 5 rooms, a boss room with the giant bat. Defeat it to win.
